video_title: Hornets vs 76ers Coach Charles Lee Postgame Media Availability | 10/31/2026

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on the difficulty of defending Tyrese Maxey
quotes.excerpt: He's a guy you got to be aware of your spatial relationship to where you are on him.
quotes.quote: He's a guy you got to be aware of your spatial relationship to where you are on him because he's so fast and so dynamic. And then as you do that, he's developed a great off-the-dribble three-point threat as well. And then he does a good job of playing off of his teammates, allowing other guys to handle and then you overshift and he punishes you for that. So, a really dynamic scorer that beats you in a lot of ways.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on defending Tyrese Maxey: He is a guy you have to be aware of your spatial relationship to because he is so fast and dynamic. He has developed a great off the dribble three point threat and punishes you for overshifting.

structured.context: Charles Lee discusses the defensive challenges posed by Tyrese Maxey during his postgame media availability.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on defensive execution and late-game turnovers
quotes.excerpt: Just the defensive intensity, the ability to finish possessions.
quotes.quote: Just the defensive intensity, the ability to finish possessions. There's a couple possessions in that fourth quarter, you allow an offensive rebound and it ends up in a kick-out three for someone, or you overshift or we don't come up with the loose ball and Tyrese Maxey is able to get it and then he's going to the free-throw line for two. So, just some of those small things in the margin, you got to be really tight with.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee points to defensive intensity and finishing possessions as the key areas for improvement after the loss to the 76ers. He noted that small things in the margin like loose balls and rebounding were the difference.

structured.context: Charles Lee explains the defensive lapses and turnovers that occurred in the fourth quarter against the 76ers.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on Grayson Allen's impact and defensive versatility
quotes.excerpt: I've been really impressed with his defensive intensity.
quotes.quote: Really good two-way player. I've been really impressed with his defensive intensity. I think he's even been able to teach some of the other guys some of his tactics that he uses with some of his swipes and shift activity. And then offensively, his shooting has always been something that's been at a premium, but today we even get to see him driving and kicking and throwing lobs and stuff. So his playmaking gives us another ball-handler out there that I think can create for himself and his teammates.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee has been impressed with Grayson Allen as a two way player. He says Allen is teaching teammates defensive tactics and providing extra playmaking as a ball handler who can create for himself and others.

structured.context: Charles Lee praises Grayson Allen for his defensive intensity and offensive playmaking abilities.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on the decision to start Grayson Allen in the second half
quotes.excerpt: It just gave us a little more balance to our lineups.
quotes.quote: It just gave us a little more balance to our lineups. What he added to that group, I thought he was playing really good defense and was going to be able to take on a certain matchup and then help the flow of our offense a little bit while also allowing Cason to give our second lineup a little bit more balance as well as another ball-handler and creator with Grayson and where Brandon was with his foul trouble, I wanted to be mindful of that.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee explains the decision to start Grayson Allen in the second half was about finding balance in the lineups and managing Brandon Miller's foul trouble while keeping a creator on the floor.

structured.context: Charles Lee explains the reasoning behind his decision to start Grayson Allen in the second half to balance the team's lineups.
